subject: Where did the pitchfork come from?
preview: Most of what people believe about hell never came from Scripture.
linkText: What Is Hell? What the Bible Actually Says

blocks.text: Maybe you grew up scared of a cartoon devil with a pitchfork.
Red suit. Horns. Flames everywhere.
And somewhere along the way, you stopped being sure how much of that is actually in the Bible.
Here is the honest answer. Most of it came from movies and medieval paintings.
Not from Scripture.
The real picture in the Bible is more careful than that.
It unfolds in stages instead of arriving all at once.
Our English Bibles often flatten several different ideas into one word, hell.
📜 Sheol, the Old Testament word for the realm of the dead
📜 Hades, the Greek word the New Testament uses the same way
📜 Gehenna, the word Jesus used for final judgment
🔥 The lake of fire, hell's final and permanent form
Each one means something a little different, and the differences actually matter.
But there is one line in Matthew 25 I do not want you to miss.
"Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels."
Prepared for the devil and his angels.
Not originally for people.
Hell was never God's desired ending for you. The cross is His answer to it.
Jesus talked about hell more than almost anyone else in Scripture.
Not to scare people for no reason. He talked about it because He loves people, and eternity is real.
That is why this is worth understanding, not avoiding.
In the full guide I walk through each word, what happens after death, where faithful Christians disagree about whether hell lasts forever, and how to comfort someone who is grieving.
It is heavy ground, so take it slow.
